dedupe_keys.name: national zoning and land use database nzlud zoning code measures for over 2 600 us municipalities

description: The National Zoning and Land Use Database (NZLUD), built at Princeton University's Eviction Lab, describes key elements of municipal zoning codes and the limits they impose for over 2,600 municipalities across the United States. It was built from publicly available zoning texts and records measures such as minimum lot size, maximum permitted density, minimum parking requirements and maximum building height. The Eviction Lab page, last updated on 27 October 2023, links the code and data on GitHub, a blog post on the method and the full article in Urban Studies, and calls the database a living resource. Coverage: national, United States, at municipality level. Format and access: tabular data and code in a public GitHub repository, free. Licence: not stated on the project page; the repository could not be read from the cloud session, so its licence file was not checked. Caveats: measures are extracted from code texts and may lag amendments; municipalities without online codes are missing. Simulation uses: agent-based and capacity planning models of housing supply and urban growth, and climate adaptation studies of where building is permitted. Related records: the National Zoning Atlas (data-national-zoning-atlas) maps zoning districts instead of summary measures.
